pr_title: Fix handling of default values in RDG
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/51183.

`IParameterSymbol.ExplicitDefaultValue` returns null when the type is a struct type and th default value of the parameter is the default value of the struct type ([ref](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.codeanalysis.iparametersymbol.explicitdefaultvalue?view=roslyn-dotnet-4.6.0)). Update the code generation to handle `IParameterSymbol.HasExplicitDefaultValue = true` and `IParameterSymbol.ExplicitDefaultValue = null`. Also fixes formating of stringified boolean default.

issue_context.title: RequestDelegateGenerator creates incorrect code with default parameters for bool and CancellationToken in Lambda expressions (AOT)
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Creating an AOT Web API project (dotnet new webapiaot), and using default parameter values in Lambda expression for bool and CancellationToken, such as the following creates invalid code.

```csharp
        group.MapGet("/", async (
            IGamesService gameService,
            string? gameType = default,
            string? playerName = default,
            DateOnly? date = default,
            bool ended = default,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) =>
        {
          //...
        });
```

This is part of the generated code:

```csharp
                var handler = Cast(del, global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults.Ok<global::System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<global::Codebreaker.GameAPIs.Models.Game>>> (global::Codebreaker.GameAPIs.Services.IGamesService arg0, global::System.String? arg1= null, global::System.String? arg2= null, global::System.DateOnly? arg3= null, global::System.Boolean arg4= False, global::System.Threading.CancellationToken arg5= null) => throw null!);
```

With the `bool` parameter, the value `False` is created which should be `false`.
With the default value for the `CancellationToken`, `null` is assigned - but this is a vlaue type.



### Expected Behavior

I would expect to create true/false for bool types, and correct defaults for value types such as CancellationToken.

### Steps To Reproduce

Create an AOT Web API project (webapiaot template)
Define an API method with bool and CancellationToken parameters, and assign default values

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

8.0.100-rc.1.23455.8

### Anything else?

In this repository
https://github.com/PacktPublishing/Pragmatic-Microservices-with-CSharp-and-Azure

in the branch requestdelegategenerator
the issue is in the folder ch05, Codebreaker.GameAPIs.NativeAOT.

review_comments:
Does `double` get handled by `_ => SymbolDisplay.FormatPrimitive`?

Did that API not handle `double.NaN`, `float.PositiveInfinity`, etc.? It claims to support all the types, so kinda odd that they need to be special cased?

Yep, the `double` is handled correctly by our terminal case. The comment on this API is rather deceptive given the conversation that is occuring in https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/58705. Evidently, `SymbolDisplay.FormatX` APIs are not intended for code gen. The recommended alternative [defined here](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/0caa880a161057559d1dcaad890e4053f520136e/src/Workspaces/Core/Portable/Editing/SyntaxGenerator.cs#L1803) is defined in the workspace layer and would require introducing some new dependencies for the generator.

Given that we've been successful using SymbolDisplay in other places (displaying FQNs) I'm incline to workaround its limitations given the finite set of types we have to deal with here.
The runtime does it like this: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/93160/files#diff-60e086268f0958325d865a75b553a6ed42b402d0a1792132e426a598172dace5R57

> The runtime does it like this: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/93160/files#diff-60e086268f0958325d865a75b553a6ed42b402d0a1792132e426a598172dace5R57

Yeah, I think using `FormatPrimitive` is a sufficient alternative to calling the converter here. In any case, I'm planning on merging this to 9.0, evaluating the fix, then putting it into a servicing release of 8.0
